Definition: from G4841; having a fellow-feeling ("sympathetic"), i.e. (by implication) mutually commiserative:--having compassion one of another.
BiblicalUsage: Peter sums up the Christian life in one line: be all of one mind, having compassion one of another, love as brethren, be pitiful, be courteous. Compassion here is not a feeling kept to yourself but a fellow-feeling that shows in how you treat the family.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that compassion toward one another is the mark of a mind made one in Christ, and I hold that a church without it has missed the point.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
